title: Milling tool flank-wear prediction from force, vibration and acoustic-emission signals
summary: Train on two fully measured cutters (315 cuts each, 7-channel 50 kHz signals plus per-cut flank wear) and predict the per-cut, per-flute flank wear of a third cutter; scored by MAE against the hidden measurements.
taskPrompt:
You are a machining process engineer building a tool-condition-monitoring model for a high-speed CNC milling operation.

## Input
- Training cutters c1 and c6 in `input/train/<cutter>/`: `cuts/cut_001.csv` ... `cut_315.csv` hold the raw signals of one cut each (about 127,000 rows sampled at 50 kHz; columns Fx_N, Fy_N, Fz_N, Vx_g, Vy_g, Vz_g, AE_RMS_V), and `wear.csv` gives the flank wear measured after each cut on the three flutes (cut,flute_1,flute_2,flute_3 in micrometres).
- Test cutter c4 in `input/test/c4/cuts/`: the same 315 cut files, but no wear file.

## What you must do
1. Engineer features from the signals and fit a model on c1 and c6.
2. Predict the flank wear of c4 after every cut for all three flutes.
3. Write `output/c4_wear_pred.csv` with header `cut,flute_1,flute_2,flute_3` and exactly 315 rows for cuts 1..315, values in micrometres.

## Scoring
MAE over the 945 predicted values: <= 6 um scores 1.0, >= 24 um scores 0.0, linear in between.
agentMustDo: Read the training signals and wear tables for c1 and c6.
Build a feature pipeline and a regression model for flank wear.
Predict all 315 cuts x 3 flutes for c4.
Write output/c4_wear_pred.csv in the required schema.

inputFiles.name: train/c1, train/c6
inputFiles.description: 315 raw cut files per cutter (7 signal columns, 50 kHz) plus wear.csv with measured flank wear per cut and flute.

inputFiles.name: test/c4/cuts
inputFiles.description: 315 raw cut files of the test cutter; wear withheld.

inputFiles.name: README.md
inputFiles.description: Task brief, column definitions, output schema.

referenceFiles.name: c4_wear.csv
referenceFiles.description: Measured flank wear of c4 after each of the 315 cuts, three flutes, micrometres.

evaluation:
**Hard gate conditions** (score = 0): output/c4_wear_pred.csv missing; not parseable; columns other than cut,flute_1,flute_2,flute_3; any cut missing, duplicated or outside 1..315; any non-numeric, NaN or infinite value.

**Scoring method:** MAE in micrometres over all 945 (cut, flute) values against the hidden reference. score = 1.0 if MAE <= 6; 0.0 if MAE >= 24; linear between. RMSE is logged for diagnostics.

- Where does the scoring logic run? host-side in evaluate(), pure Python; only two file reads touch the VM.

**PERFECT output:** predictions within 6 um MAE of the measurements, score 1.0 (the 2010 challenge leaders reached single-digit MAE).
**WRONG/empty output:** missing file, malformed CSV, or a constant guess (MAE about 36 um): score 0. Averaging the two training cutters by cut index without touching the signals gives MAE about 18 um, score about 0.3.
